title: The ocean between us
author: Weather Commons · Pilot 01
description: Follow a passive tracer through an idealized Atlantic circulation. Change the conditions. Watch another geography emerge.

source.title: Idealized Atlantic transport · v1
source.note: Synthetic stationary wind field, midpoint integration and seeded random-walk diffusion. Inspired by Lagrangian transport methods; not HYSPLIT output, observed weather, or a forecast. Height evolves by idealized vertical diffusion with reflecting boundaries at 0 and 12 km above a smooth reference sphere. The same horizontal wind applies at every height. No vertical wind, wind shear, terrain, chemistry, cloud physics or rain prediction.

chapters.label: 01 / RELEASE
chapters.title: A point of departure
chapters.text: A cloud of 2,400 passive tracers starts east of the North American coast. Every point starts at 3 km above the reference sphere, with a location, a clock, and the same initial weight. This release is a thought experiment.

chapters.label: 02 / TRANSPORT
chapters.title: An atmosphere in motion
chapters.text: A prescribed jet and rotating circulation carry the tracers east. The trajectories are calculated, not prerecorded. Wind speed changes their travel; diffusion changes their spread.

chapters.label: 03 / OBSERVATION
chapters.title: The gaps between instruments
chapters.text: The Azores anchor this stop in a real geography. An observing-network registry can tell us what instruments exist; it cannot alone tell us which observations a particular model used.

chapters.label: 04 / KNOWLEDGE
chapters.title: Where a field becomes a forecast
chapters.text: ECMWF combines observations with model information to estimate the atmospheric state. Our synthetic field exposes the interface mechanics; an observational contribution must bring its own provenance.

chapters.label: 05 / COMMONS
chapters.title: A shared sky. Unequal knowledge.
chapters.text: Which institutions can observe this movement? Who can calculate it, act on it, or contest its description? Export this experiment with its assumptions and build another account.
